standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the exact sequence 0 -> omega_C -> omega_X|_C -> O_{C cap X'} -> 0 on which the degree computation runs.

standard_prerequisites.name: The rational tail as a projective line over an extension field
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Example example-rational-tail and Proposition proposition-projective-line
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies C with P^1_{k'}, so deg(omega_C) = -2[k' : k], and fixes the intersection degree deg(C cap X') = [k' : k].

core_obligations: Dualizing exact sequence (proof lines 5994-6001): with X' the closed subscheme of the example, the short exact sequence 0 -> omega_C -> omega_X|_C -> O_{C cap X'} -> 0 holds by the three nodal-curve lemmas.

Degree computation (proof lines 6002-6007): C is isomorphic to P^1_{k'} by proposition-projective-line, so deg(omega_C) = -2[k' : k]; the conductor intersection has degree deg(C cap X') = [k' : k]; additivity of degrees in the exact sequence yields deg(omega_X|_C) = -[k' : k], which is negative.
proof_roadmap: Set up the dualizing short exact sequence along the rational tail and its complement.
Compute both boundary degrees via the P^1_{k'} identification and additivity to conclude negativity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the restriction of the dualizing sheaf to a rational tail has strictly negative degree (statement lines 5986-5992). The proof (lines 5994-6007) runs an actual degree computation inside the span: the conductor exact sequence from the nodal-subscheme lemmas, the identification of the tail with P^1 over the extension field k' giving deg(omega_C) = -2[k' : k], the intersection degree [k' : k], and the additive conclusion deg(omega_X|_C) = -[k' : k] < 0. H2: compact, but the degree bookkeeping is the argument and it feeds the rational-tail contraction results that the stable-model section is built on.
